$comment: Banned dependencies. Keys are npm package names as pnpm-lock.yaml records them in its packages section; the checker scans the full lockfile (transitive included), so a ban here blocks any path of arrival. Extend with a reason - a ban without one will be questioned at review. Advisory acceptance (vulnerabilities that are accepted rather than bans) lives in pnpm-workspace.yaml auditConfig.ignoreGhsas - pnpm's native mechanism, mirrored here because JSON cannot carry comments: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm (CVE-2026-93687, high, braces stack-exhaustion DoS on deeply nested patterns) has no patched release (braces@3.0.3 is the latest) and cannot be dropped from the tree; it arrives via micromatch@4 from deepagents (production; the framework's glob pattern and grep glob filter are model-supplied, including from delegated subagents) and the web lint toolchain (dev; repo-owned config). The model-supplied args are the only request-controlled input to the matcher and are bounded by GuardedFilesystemBackend in driver-deepagents (<= 1024 chars, <= 32 brace-nesting depth, <= 1024 brace expansions; sequential groups multiply, alternatives add, escaped braces are not structure): deepagents shares that one backend instance between the root agent and every generated subagent, while root custom middleware is not merged into subagents, so the guard has to live at the backend boundary; re-check on any braces, micromatch, deepagents, or eslint-config-next bump, and if the guard no longer covers the framework's pattern entry points.
